title: Cyclotomic residues of $\Phi_q \cdot \mathrm{tr}_{M, \ell}$ — algebraic definition
html:
Proposition. Cyclotomic residues of \Phi_q \cdot \mathrm{tr}_{M, \ell} — algebraic definition

Proposition (conditional on conj:gs-residue-at-root-existence). Let T_w \in J^\ell / J^{\ell+1} have \mathrm{tr}_{M, \ell}(T_w) \in \mathbb{Q}(q). The cyclotomic residue

  \mathrm{Res}_{q \to \zeta_\ell}(\Phi_q \cdot \mathrm{tr}_{M, \ell})(T_w)

is the image of \Phi_q \cdot \mathrm{tr}_{M, \ell}(T_w) under the cyclotomic projection

  \pi_{n_\ell}
  \;:\;
  \widehat{\mathbb{Z}[q]}
  \longrightarrow
  \mathbb{Z}[q] / \Phi_{n_\ell}(q),

evaluating identically within the residue field \mathbb{Q}(\zeta_\ell).

The cyclotomic residue is defined purely algebraically within the Habiro completion of \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}]. It avoids complex-analytic limits entirely. The formulation keeps the algebraic sector strictly within \mathbb{Q}-coefficients, fulfilling the three-calibration discipline.

The conjectural hypothesis is the existence of the cyclotomic projection \pi_{n_\ell} on the Habiro completion — the content of conj:gs-residue-at-root-existence, axiomatised as the Lean class ResidueAtRoot (fields: the target ring family and the projection ring homomorphism). Conditional on an instance of that class, the statement above is derived: the residue is the image of \Phi_q \cdot \mathrm{tr}_{M,\ell}(T_w) under \pi_{n_\ell}, realised by a ring homomorphism into \mathbb{Z}[q]/\Phi_{n_\ell}(q).
